title: Arranging for Ethel Waters and 'Supper Time'
summary: Whaley first arranged for Ethel Waters at the Lafayette Theatre for $12, and Hinton says he made records with her.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: Oh, Ethel to me was a great -- I remember the first time I saw her, at the Lafayette Theater. And I said, Ethel, you need some music. And she said, my piano player would tell them all what to do. I said, no, you got too much to learn. You can't keep it in your head.
Anyway, she consented. I think she only give me 12 dollars.
Oh, yeah. But Ethel was a great -- I remember she was singing 'Supper Time'.
I'm lucky to be able to say that through the graces of you and MR. Eddie Mallory and Tyre and Benny Carter. I got to make some records with her.
Oh, a few of them, 'Bread and Gravy' and a couple of things that she did back in the '30s and the early '40s.
Did you -- did she do 'Supper Time' with you?
No, I don't think I did 'Supper Time' with her.
That's when she's talking about her old man won't come back anymore.
